coverage: Dinesh Varyani's 'Crack The Coding Interview - Must Do Questions (1-500)': a 500-row spreadsheet (#, LeetCode topic tags, LeetCode problem link, difficulty; 131 Easy, 296 Medium, 73 Hard), apparently ordered by priority, with Two Sum first. No explanations, hints or solutions; the header only credits the author and his YouTube channel and states no licence. Its value is as a curated, ranked practice backlog; 'page' here is the row number.

refs.title: Array and Hash Table questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: The bulk of the list: about 250 array and 90 hash-table rows, mostly Medium. A plain checklist of LeetCode links, no hints; useful for picking which array/hashing classics to practise next.

refs.title: String questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: About 106 string rows (30 Easy, 55 Medium, 21 Hard), spanning parsing, palindromes, anagrams and matching. Links only; handy for spotting string classics to add.

refs.title: Sliding Window questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 21 rows tagged sliding window, skewed Medium/Hard (longest substring, minimum window, window maximum). Links only, no explanation.

refs.title: Two Pointers questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 56 two-pointer rows from easy pair sums to 3Sum/4Sum, trapping water and in-place array edits. A checklist, not a lesson.

refs.title: Dynamic Programming questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: About 107 DP rows (plus memoization tags), 70 Medium and 28 Hard: knapsack, grid paths, string DP, stock trading, interval DP. Untagged by sub-pattern; links only.

refs.title: DP sub-patterns by name
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: The list does not tag DP families, but by name it covers Fibonacci-style (stairs, robbers), 0/1 and unbounded knapsack (partition, coin change), palindromic and LCS/edit-distance problems.

refs.title: Linked List questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 35 linked-list rows: reversal (whole, between, k-group), merging, cycle detection, copy with random pointer, reorder. Links only.

refs.title: Cycle / middle questions (fast & slow)
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Not a tag in the list, but rows such as the duplicate-number, list-cycle I/II, middle-of-list, happy-number and palindrome-list problems are the fast/slow pointer family.

refs.title: Recursion and Divide-and-Conquer questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: About 21 recursion and 23 divide-and-conquer rows (median of two arrays, tree construction, sort list, burst balloons). Divide and conquer has no catalog topic of its own.

refs.title: Math questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 53 math rows: digit manipulation, primes, powers and roots, number conversions, a few combinatorics/geometry/game-theory items. Mostly Easy/Medium.

refs.title: Sorting questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 54 sorting rows plus bucket/merge/quickselect/radix tags (top-k, intervals, custom orders, sort an array). Links only.

refs.title: Binary Search questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 47 binary-search rows, 12 of them Hard: rotated arrays, first/last position, peak finding, search-on-answer (ship capacity, Koko, split array).

refs.title: Greedy questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 37 greedy rows, almost all Medium (jump game, gas station, partition labels, task scheduler, interval arrows). A good backlog source for greedy practice.

refs.title: Depth-First Search questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: About 97 DFS rows, mostly tree and grid recursion, plus graph cloning and path enumeration. Overlaps heavily with the tree group.

refs.title: Breadth-First Search questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: About 71 BFS rows: level-order tree traversals, grid shortest paths, word ladder, open-the-lock, rotting oranges. Links only.

refs.title: Matrix / grid traversal questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 44 matrix rows; the grid-flood ones (islands, surrounded regions, Pacific-Atlantic, shortest bridge) fit our islands pattern. Others are matrix simulation (rotate, spiral, game of life).

refs.title: Union Find questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 16 union-find rows (islands, provinces, redundant connection, accounts merge, stones removed), mostly Medium.

refs.title: Design questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 23 design rows: LRU/LFU caches, min stack, iterators, randomized set, time-based store, Twitter, hash map, calendars, plus data-stream items.

refs.title: Backtracking questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 29 backtracking rows (permutations, combinations, subsets, N-Queens, sudoku, word search, IP addresses); no Easy items.

refs.title: Bit Manipulation questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 26 bit rows: single-number family (XOR), counting bits, reverse bits, power of two, complement, sum without plus, maximum XOR.

refs.title: Prefix Sum questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 13 prefix-sum rows (subarray sum equals k, product except self, contiguous array, divisible-by-k, range sum queries).

refs.title: Heap (Priority Queue) questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 32 heap rows, 11 Hard: k-th largest/smallest, top-k frequent, merging k lists, running median, scheduling and skyline.

refs.title: Merging sorted sources
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: By name: merge k lists, k-th smallest in sorted matrix, smallest range over k lists, k smallest pairs (k-way merge) and median of a stream, sliding-window median (two heaps).

refs.title: Trie questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 11 trie rows (implement trie, word search II, add-and-search words, search suggestions, palindrome pairs, concatenated words).

refs.title: Tree and BST questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: About 80 binary-tree and 23 BST rows: traversals, depth/diameter, LCA, construction, serialization, validation, k-th smallest, path sums.

refs.title: Stack and Monotonic Stack questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 45 stack rows, 16 of them monotonic (histogram, daily temperatures, next greater, stock span), plus parsing (decode string, calculators, RPN).

refs.title: Interval questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: Not tagged, but by name: merge, insert, non-overlapping intervals, interval intersections, my-calendar booking, arrows to burst balloons, car pooling.

refs.title: Missing/duplicate number questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: By name: find the duplicate, first missing positive, numbers disappeared, all duplicates, set mismatch, missing number: the cyclic-sort family.

refs.title: Graph, Topological Sort and Shortest Path questions
refs.subject: algo
refs.summary: 22 general graph rows: course schedules (topological sort), network delay, cheapest flights, swim in water, path with minimum effort, plus bridges and itinerary (Eulerian path).
